title: Chapter 93 — The Review Rituals: Daily, Weekly, Quarterly
intro: The daily close, the weekly review, the quarterly deep-dive — the rhythm that keeps your business on track.

sections.title: The Daily Close
sections.content:
At the end of every day, take five minutes. Log your customers. Note your wins and misses. Set tomorrow's priorities. Update your CRM.

This is not optional. This is how you prevent small problems from becoming big ones. A quote you forgot to follow up on today becomes a lost sale by Friday.

sections.title: The Weekly Review
sections.content:
Once a week — same day, same time — review your numbers. Closing percentage. Number of customers. Average ticket. Follow-ups made. Pipeline status.

Ask yourself: what went well? What did I miss? What one thing will I focus on improving next week?

The weekly review is where patterns emerge. One bad day is noise. Three bad days in a row is a signal.

sections.title: The Quarterly Deep-Dive
sections.content:
Every quarter, zoom out. Look at three months of data. Are you trending up or down? Which product categories are growing? Where are your sales coming from — walk-ins, referrals, follow-ups, online?

The quarterly review is where strategy happens. It is where you decide whether to invest more time in a product category, deepen your trade relationships, or focus on base management.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating review rituals, ask:

Does the salesperson close out every day with a review — or just leave?
Do they conduct weekly reviews of their own metrics?
Do they zoom out quarterly to look at trends and strategy?
Are they using reviews to improve — or just checking a box?
